entries.clue: The fellow twitching, having caught cold, becoming feverish (6)

indicatorNotes.having caught: TIC has caught C, holding it at its front edge

blocks.note: C = cold, as on a tap
a tic is a twitching of a muscle

annotation.surface: A man shivering with a chill is running a temperature.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'feverish' sound like a symptom of the chill; it is the definition, using the word's older medical sense, as in a hectic flush.
annotation.definitionFit: Hectic originally described the flushed, feverish state of a consumptive patient.

entries.clue: Rude in food shop, provide grub not right (10)

indicatorNotes.not right: R, the abbreviation for right, is removed from CATER

annotation.surface: Someone behaves badly in a delicatessen while the kitchen serves the wrong food.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link placing the rudeness in a shop, but it is the first two letters of the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Indelicate means coarse or tactless, which is to say rude.

entries.clue: Dissolute ten-year period not without love (8)

indicatorNotes.without love: love is O, the zero score in tennis, and NOT loses it

annotation.surface: A wild decade that was anything but loveless.
annotation.walkthrough: 'not without' reads as a double negative meaning 'with', but 'not' is the fodder and 'without love' is the instruction to drop O.
annotation.definitionFit: Decadent describes self-indulgent moral decline, the same as dissolute.

entries.clue: Dog in street running wild (6)

indicatorNotes.running wild: the letters of STREET run wild into a new order

annotation.surface: A loose dog is tearing about in the road.
annotation.walkthrough: The dog running wild in the street is a complete picture; the answer is also the crossword word for the compiler.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Irish or English setter is one breed of dog, named for crouching or 'setting' when it finds game.

entries.clue: What could make one staid? (8)

indicatorNotes.could make: ONE STAID could be made into another arrangement of its letters

annotation.surface: A question about what would calm a person down.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: sedation is indeed what makes one staid.
annotation.definitionFit: Sedation calms a person, making them quiet and sober, or staid.

entries.clue: Reckless person showing sign of sorrow far from home? (8)

blocks.note: away = not at home, as in an away match

annotation.surface: A wild youngster crying because they are a long way from home.
annotation.walkthrough: TEAR here is the drop from the eye, not a rip, though the answer then puts it back to the rushing sense.
annotation.definitionFit: A mainly British word for a wild youth who tears about heedless of danger, so a plain synonym for reckless person.

entries.clue: One of a bygone age found up a tree (8)

annotation.definition: One of a bygone age found up a tree

blocks.note: the surface pushes a prehistoric creature; the setter means a forebear from an earlier generation
not a creature in the branches but a name higher up a family tree

annotation.surface: A prehistoric creature perched in a tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The tree is a family tree, and going up it takes you back through the generations to ancestors.
annotation.definitionFit: An ancestor lived in an earlier age and sits higher on the family tree.

entries.clue: Walk when there’s no parking for vehicle (4)

indicatorNotes.when there’s no: TRAMP is taken without its P

blocks.note: to tramp is to walk heavily
P = parking, as on road signs; it is removed

annotation.surface: A complaint that you have to go on foot when you can't park the car.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface puts parking with the car, but P comes off the walking word, not the vehicle.
annotation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle running on rails in the street.

entries.clue: List revealing old books collected by artist (4)

indicatorNotes.collected by: the artist's letters collect OT between them

blocks.note: RA = Royal Academician, an artist; it holds the books
OT = Old Testament, the old books of the Bible

annotation.surface: A catalogue of antique books gathered by a painter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'old books' is OT, the Old Testament, not antiques; RA is the usual artist.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, chiefly British: a rota is the duty list saying whose turn it is, from Latin for wheel.

entries.clue: 22 ultimately ruined our planet (6)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: take the final letter of ruined

annotation.surface: A lament that the world has been wrecked in the end.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is a cross-reference: 22 across is SHORTAGE, and a dearth is a shortage.
annotation.definitionFit: A dearth is a scarcity, which is what SHORTAGE (22) means.

entries.clue: Group needing a role isolated from others (3,5)

blocks.note: a part in a play is a role

annotation.surface: An actor in a troupe feels left out because they have no role.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one sad actor; each word of the wordplay simply lines up in order.
annotation.definitionFit: Set apart means separated or isolated from the rest.

entries.clue: Old right-winger and that revolutionary leading ceremony (11)

blocks.note: Che Guevara, the crossword's usual revolutionary

annotation.surface: A conservative veteran and a revolutionary leading a ceremony together.
annotation.walkthrough: A Thatcherite is a follower of Margaret Thatcher, UK Conservative prime minister 1979-90. 'leading' looks like the revolutionary running the ceremony; it only fixes the order.
annotation.definitionFit: Thatcherites were supporters of the right-wing policies of Margaret Thatcher.

entries.clue: Recollected tales again in English region (4,6)

indicatorNotes.Recollected: read as re-collected: TALES AGAIN gathered up in a new order

annotation.surface: Old stories remembered and retold in a rural part of England.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Recollected' looks like memory, which suits 'tales again', but it means collected afresh. East Anglia is the eastern bulge of England: Norfolk, Suffolk and around.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the old Anglo-Saxon kingdom, now Norfolk, Suffolk and parts of Cambridgeshire, is one of England's regions.

entries.clue: Put in harm’s way, stop getting cross (8)

blocks.note: cross = angry; ANGER is the noun

annotation.surface: Stepping in to break up a quarrel puts you at risk.
annotation.walkthrough: 'cross' has to be heard as a mood, not a mark or a crossing.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, verb for verb: the phrase is simply an idiomatic way of saying expose to danger.

entries.clue: Criminal activity? I attempt to go after gang (8)

indicatorNotes.to go after: I TRY is placed after BAND

annotation.surface: A would-be crook wonders whether to chase after a gang.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has someone pursuing a gang; 'go after' is only a placing instruction, and the question mark warns that the definition is an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example, flagged by the question mark: highway robbery by armed gangs is one kind of crime among many.

entries.clue: Fruit very large found across farm complex? (7)

indicatorNotes.found across: OS is found stretched across RANGE

blocks.note: OS = outsize, a clothing size label
a range is a large ranch or grazing area; the ? admits the stretch

annotation.surface: Giant fruit growing over a farmyard.
annotation.walkthrough: OS for outsize is a clothing label convention. RANGE, the open grazing land of a ranch, sits inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the plural noun names one citrus kind, and 'Fruit' works as a plural too.

entries.clue: Component of toothpaste could bring a tingle somehow to end of tongue (8)

indicatorNotes.somehow: A TINGLE is rearranged in some way
indicatorNotes.to: E is added to the anagram

annotation.surface: Toothpaste leaving a tingle on the tip of the tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'end of tongue' sounds like the tip where you feel the tingle; here it is the last letter E.
annotation.definitionFit: Gelatine is used as a thickener in some toothpastes.

entries.clue: Girl about ten gets device for picking up signals (7)

annotation.surface: A ten-year-old girl is given a radio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'about ten' reads as an approximate age; it is the container instruction.
annotation.definitionFit: An antenna is an aerial for receiving radio signals.

entries.clue: Chart with names provided as a matter of course? (11)

annotation.definition: Chart with names provided as a matter of course?

blocks.note: a board listing names in ranked order

blocks.clueFragment: provided as a matter of course?
blocks.note: the surface says routinely; the setter means supplied at a golf course

annotation.surface: A register of names drawn up routinely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'as a matter of course' seems to mean routinely, but the course is a golf course, where a leaderboard lists the players' names and scores.
annotation.definitionFit: A leaderboard is the scoreboard of names at a golf tournament.

entries.clue: Report of e.g. Shakespeare being banned (6)

indicatorNotes.Report of: a report is what is heard, so the word is spoken

annotation.surface: News that Shakespeare has been censored.
annotation.walkthrough: 'e.g.' flags that Shakespeare is one example of a bard; in non-rhotic British speech BARD and BARRED sound the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both past participles: a bar across a door keeps people out, as a ban does.

entries.clue: Goddess is making repeat appearance (4)

indicatorNotes.making repeat appearance: a repeat appearance is a second showing, so IS turns up once more straight after itself

annotation.surface: A goddess returns for an encore.
annotation.walkthrough: Isis is the Egyptian mother goddess.
annotation.definitionFit: Isis was a major goddess of ancient Egypt.

entries.clue: What sounds like only person (4)

indicatorNotes.sounds like: the answer is spoken the same as the word for only

blocks.note: sole = only, as in sole survivor

annotation.surface: A question about which word matches a lone individual.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is person, as in 'not a soul'; 'only' gives SOLE, which is said the same.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: the word counts people in phrases like 'not a soul in sight' and 'a hundred souls aboard'.

entries.clue: Brief period that may produce famine (8)

blocks.note: an age is a period of time

annotation.surface: A short spell of scarcity could lead to hunger.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a cause-and-effect story; 'that may produce' is only the link, and famine is itself a shortage of food.
annotation.definitionFit: A famine is an extreme shortage, above all of food.

entries.clue: Alarm should be loud, correct? (6)

annotation.surface: Someone checks that an alarm bell is loud enough.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads Alarm as a bell; it is the feeling of fear. F for loud comes from musical notation (forte).
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, noun for noun: the sudden fear you feel when startled, as in 'you gave me an alarm'.

entries.clue: Magnificent little man performed on second piano (8)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across answer, LEN DID comes on (after) S P

blocks.note: did = performed, as in did a dance

annotation.surface: A short man gave a superb performance on a second piano.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a pianist, but 'piano' is just P and 'on' puts the man's part after S P.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, adjective for adjective: both describe something grand and dazzling, from Latin splendere, to shine.

entries.clue: Ready, when troubled, to embrace learner with affection (6)

indicatorNotes.when troubled: READY is disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: L = learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

annotation.surface: An anxious driving instructor still hugs a student warmly.
annotation.walkthrough: READY is scrambled to DEARY, which takes L inside it.
annotation.definitionFit: Dearly means with deep affection, as in loved dearly.
